label: Cybersecurity, Malware, Privacy and Global Outages
blurb: A focused six-fact drill set for Cybersecurity, Malware, Privacy and Global Outages.

topics.title: Cybersecurity
topics.hook: Cybersecurity protects systems, networks, and data from unauthorised access, attack, or disruption.
topics.explainer: Cybersecurity protects systems, networks, and data from unauthorised access, attack, or disruption. It is a useful TCS Quiz recall point because questions often test the term, person, date, or application together.
topics.category: Cybersecurity, Malware, Privacy and Global Outages

connections.fact: Cybersecurity includes training and technical controls to stop phishing messages from stealing credentials.
DDoS mitigation is a cybersecurity task focused on keeping a service reachable despite malicious traffic.

topics.title: Phishing
topics.hook: Phishing uses deceptive messages or sites to trick people into disclosing sensitive information.
topics.explainer: Phishing uses deceptive messages or sites to trick people into disclosing sensitive information. It is a useful TCS Quiz recall point because questions often test the term, person, date, or application together.
topics.category: Cybersecurity, Malware, Privacy and Global Outages

connections.fact: Attackers often use a deceptive email or site to steal credentials or deliver the malware that begins a ransomware intrusion.
A successful phishing attempt can expose login details and personal data, directly undermining privacy.

topics.title: Ransomware
topics.hook: Ransomware is malware that encrypts or blocks data access and demands payment.
topics.explainer: Ransomware is malware that encrypts or blocks data access and demands payment. It is a useful TCS Quiz recall point because questions often test the term, person, date, or application together.
topics.category: Cybersecurity, Malware, Privacy and Global Outages

connections.fact: Ransomware applies encryption to deny the owner access; legitimate encryption protects data for authorised users.
Phishing describes the deception used to gain access, while ransomware is the extortion malware that may follow.

topics.title: Encryption
topics.hook: Encryption transforms readable plaintext into protected ciphertext that authorised parties can decrypt.
topics.explainer: Encryption transforms readable plaintext into protected ciphertext that authorised parties can decrypt. It is a useful TCS Quiz recall point because questions often test the term, person, date, or application together.
topics.category: Cybersecurity, Malware, Privacy and Global Outages

connections.fact: Encryption can protect stored or transmitted personal information, although privacy also requires rules about lawful collection and use.
Both may encrypt files, but defenders retain authorised keys whereas ransomware attackers withhold access for payment.

topics.title: Data privacy
topics.hook: Data privacy governs how personal information is collected, used, stored, and shared.
topics.explainer: Data privacy governs how personal information is collected, used, stored, and shared. It is a useful TCS Quiz recall point because questions often test the term, person, date, or application together.
topics.category: Cybersecurity, Malware, Privacy and Global Outages

connections.fact: Privacy governs appropriate handling of personal data; encryption is one technical control that supports confidentiality.
Phishing can trick a person into surrendering credentials or identity information that privacy practices are meant to protect.

topics.title: Distributed denial of service
topics.hook: A distributed denial-of-service attack overwhelms a service using traffic from many systems.
topics.explainer: A distributed denial-of-service attack overwhelms a service using traffic from many systems. It is a useful TCS Quiz recall point because questions often test the term, person, date, or application together.
topics.category: Cybersecurity, Malware, Privacy and Global Outages

links.label: Distributed denial of service encyclopedia entry
Distributed denial of service reference search

connections.relationship: Availability attack within the security triad
connections.fact: DDoS attacks target availability, one of the central properties that cybersecurity seeks to preserve.
DDoS floods a service from many systems, while ransomware blocks access by compromising and encrypting data or devices.

options: Protecting systems, networks, and data from attack
questions.explanation: Cybersecurity protects confidentiality, integrity, and availability through people, processes, and technical safeguards.

questions.q: An email imitates a bank and links to a fake login page. What attack is this?
questions.explanation: Phishing uses deceptive messages and websites to make a victim reveal credentials or run malicious content.

questions.q: Which behaviour defines ransomware most directly?
options: It blocks or encrypts data and demands payment
It secretly mines cryptocurrency without an extortion demand
It records keystrokes to steal credentials
It recruits a device into a traffic-flooding botnet
questions.explanation: Ransomware is extortion malware: access is denied and restoration is offered in exchange for money, often without any guarantee.

questions.q: Readable plaintext becomes what after encryption?
questions.explanation: Encryption transforms plaintext into ciphertext that should be intelligible only with the authorised cryptographic key.

questions.q: Which question is principally about data privacy rather than service availability?
options: Why was my location collected and shared?
Can the service recover from a traffic flood?
Were account records altered without permission?
Can an authorised user retrieve the backup?
questions.explanation: Privacy concerns the legitimate collection, purpose, retention, and sharing of personal information such as location data.

questions.q: Thousands of compromised devices flood one site until genuine users cannot connect. Identify the attack.
questions.explanation: A DDoS attack coordinates traffic from many systems to exhaust a target and damage service availability.

questions.q: How can phishing and ransomware be related without being synonyms?
options: Phishing may deliver ransomware or stolen access
questions.explanation: Phishing is the deception or delivery route; ransomware is the malware-driven extortion that may follow initial access.

options: Legitimate encryption protects authorised access; ransomware withholds access
questions.explanation: The cryptographic operation can be similar, but purpose and key control distinguish a safeguard from a ransomware attack.

questions.q: A company encrypts records but collects them without a lawful purpose. What remains unresolved?
questions.explanation: Encryption supports confidentiality, but privacy also demands lawful purpose, minimisation, retention limits, and accountable use.

questions.q: Which security property is the main target of a DDoS flood?
questions.explanation: By preventing legitimate users from reaching a service, denial-of-service attacks principally undermine availability.
